title: Open subschemes of a proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $\overline C$ be a
proper smooth connected curve over $k$, and let
$j:U\hookrightarrow\overline C$ be an open immersion with
$\overline C\setminus U\neq\emptyset$. Then $U$ is affine.

proof.text: If $U=\varnothing$, it is affine as $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$. Otherwise $U$ contains the generic point $\eta$ of $\overline C$: every nonempty open of an integral scheme contains its generic point. Put $S=\overline C\setminus U$. The curve is Noetherian and integral, and every point other than $\eta$ is closed, by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Thus every point of the closed subset $S$ is closed. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite], $S$ is finite; it is nonempty by the hypothesis $U\ne\overline C$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09ND (one-dimensional Noetherian schemes), proof; the finite closed-boundary argument

proof.text: For the finite nonempty set $S$ of step 1, form the effective divisor $D=\sum_{P\in S}[P]$ of [def-sc-divisor]. Each closed point with its reduced structure is an effective Cartier divisor, and finite sums remain effective Cartier, by [lem-sc-point-cartier] and the notion in [def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor]. The support of this sum is exactly $S$, since every coefficient is one. By the divisor-degree formula in [def-sc-divisor], $\deg D=\sum_{P\in S}1=|S|>0$.

source.place: node lem-sc-affine-open-proper, Proof, first half (the finite boundary divisor)

proof.text: The divisor-class identification [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve] supplies the invertible sheaf $\mathcal O_{\overline C}(D)$. By the defining degree formula in [def-sc-pic0], $\deg[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(D)]=\deg D=|S|>0$; the well-definedness of this degree is the separate fact [lem-sc-deg-principal-zero].

source.place: node lem-sc-affine-open-proper, Proof, degree of the divisor line bundle

proof.text: The proper smooth connected curve $\overline C$ and its invertible sheaf $\mathcal O_{\overline C}(D)$ satisfy [lem-sc-positive-degree-ample], because step 3 gives positive degree; hence this sheaf is ample. By [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc], applied to the effective divisor $D$ of step 2, this sheaf $\mathcal O_{\overline C}(D)$ of [def-sc-divisor] is isomorphic to the sheaf $\mathcal O_{\overline C}(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] attached to the effective Cartier divisor $D$, so the latter is ample as well. The effective Cartier divisor $D$ from step 2 therefore satisfies [lem-sc-ample-complement-affine], so $\overline C\setminus D$ is affine. Its underlying complement is $\overline C\setminus S=U$, proving the claim also when $U$ is nonempty.

source.place: node lem-sc-affine-open-proper, Proof, final two sentences (ampleness and affine complement)
